arxiv-2404-16130-graphrag-2024.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
provenance: Verified arXiv abstract page metadata (citation_title/citation_author/citation_arxiv_id 2404.16130) and PDF body pages 1-14 read locally via pdftotext.

Abstract and method sections describe GraphRAG: LLM-built entity knowledge graph, Leiden hierarchical community detection, pregenerated community summaries, and map-reduce query answering for global sensemaking over ~1M-token corpora.

Evaluation section reports head-to-head LLM-judged comprehensiveness win rates 72-83% and diversity 62-82% vs conventional vector RAG on Podcast and News datasets, with Directness as a control criterion.

distilling-100b-models-40x-faster-with-t.label: Distilling 100B+ Models 40x Faster with TRL
distilling-100b-models-40x-faster-with-t.summary: Hugging Face research article/Space presenting TRL on-policy distillation for 100B+ teacher models, centered on generation buffering, batched vLLM teacher-server logprob requests, and binary logprob payload encoding.

trl-distillation-trainer.label: TRL DistillationTrainer
trl-distillation-trainer.summary: Experimental TRL trainer imported from trl.experimental.distillation for distilling teacher language models into student models with configurable on/off-policy data, KL/JSD-style loss settings, vLLM rollout generation, and optional external teacher server support.

on-policy-distillation.label: On-policy distillation
on-policy-distillation.summary: Distillation setup where the student generates its own rollouts during training while the teacher scores those exact rollouts with log-probabilities, letting the student learn from self-generated mistakes instead of only imitating teacher trajectories.

off-policy-distillation.label: Off-policy distillation
off-policy-distillation.summary: Distillation setup where a teacher generates completions for prompts and the student trains on those teacher-generated trajectories, using hard generated tokens or soft teacher output distributions.

generation-buffer.label: Generation buffer
generation-buffer.summary: Throughput optimization that accumulates prompts across a gradient-accumulation window, generates student rollouts in one larger vLLM batch, then consumes buffered rollouts through sequential forward/backward training steps without changing the policy before the optimizer step.

teacher-server-logprob-serving.label: Teacher-server logprob serving
teacher-server-logprob-serving.summary: External vLLM teacher server pattern where training workers query a large teacher model for token-level log-probabilities, enabling 100B+ teachers that cannot be colocated with student training GPUs.

request-batching-for-teacher-logprobs.label: Request batching for teacher logprobs
request-batching-for-teacher-logprobs.summary: Server-side batching layer that queues concurrent worker requests for a few milliseconds or until sequence/token limits are reached, combines them into one vLLM call, and splits results back to workers, reducing tail latency by about 10x in the article's setup.

binary-logprob-encoding.label: Binary logprob encoding
binary-logprob-encoding.summary: Payload optimization that packs top-k log-probabilities and token IDs into preallocated NumPy arrays shaped (batch, max_completion_len, top_k), base64-encodes them for JSON transport, and avoids nested list/Pydantic overhead.

top-k-kl-approximation.label: Top-k KL approximation
top-k-kl-approximation.summary: Approximation that computes distillation divergence over only the highest-probability token IDs at each step because full-vocabulary logprob comparison can require massive tensors, e.g. about 150 million log-probabilities for a 1k-token Qwen sample with a 150k vocabulary.

forward-kl-divergence.label: Forward KL divergence
forward-kl-divergence.summary: Divergence direction used in distillation where the teacher distribution is treated as the reference; with top-k approximation, the compared token IDs are selected from the teacher's highest log-probabilities.

reverse-kl-divergence.label: Reverse KL divergence
reverse-kl-divergence.summary: Divergence direction used in distillation that focuses on student log-probabilities; with top-k approximation, the compared token IDs are selected from the student's highest log-probabilities.

capacity-gap-in-distillation.label: Capacity gap in distillation
capacity-gap-in-distillation.summary: Observed limitation where a much larger teacher does not always yield proportionally better students because the smaller student may not absorb all additional teacher capability; the article reports similar AIME25 distilled-student levels from 30B and 235B Qwen teachers and a GPQA drop with the 235B teacher after step 40.

domain-specific-reasoning-distillation.label: Domain-specific reasoning distillation
domain-specific-reasoning-distillation.summary: Using distillation to transfer targeted capabilities such as bushcraft/survival behavior or math reasoning from larger teachers into smaller deployable students, including experiments with Gemma 4 and Qwen3 teachers/students.

vllm-batched-inference-engine.label: vLLM batched inference engine
vllm-batched-inference-engine.summary: Inference engine used for efficient student rollout generation and external teacher logprob serving; the article's optimizations are framed around recovering vLLM batching efficiency during training and teacher-server requests.

qwen3-235b-teacher-distillation.label: Qwen3 235B teacher distillation
qwen3-235b-teacher-distillation.summary: Example large-teacher setup using Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 as a teacher to distill capabilities into Qwen/Qwen3-4B, motivated by moving behavior from a model requiring roughly 400GB memory into a much smaller deployable student.

graphrag-query-focused-summarization.label: GraphRAG (Graph RAG)
graphrag-query-focused-summarization.summary: Graph-based RAG approach that answers global sensemaking questions over an entire private corpus by building an LLM-derived entity knowledge graph, partitioning it into a hierarchy of communities, pregenerating community summaries, and answering queries via map-reduce over those summaries.

global-sensemaking-qfs.label: Global sensemaking / query-focused summarization
global-sensemaking-qfs.summary: Class of queries directed at an entire corpus (e.g. 'What are the main themes?') that require reasoning over connections across the whole dataset rather than retrieving a few relevant chunks; framed as query-focused summarization (QFS) rather than explicit retrieval.

conventional-vector-rag.label: Conventional vector RAG
conventional-vector-rag.summary: Baseline retrieval-augmented generation that fetches text chunks most similar to a query into the LLM context window; effective for local fact-finding but unable to support sensemaking over an entire corpus when the source exceeds the context window.

entity-knowledge-graph-index.label: LLM-derived entity knowledge graph index
entity-knowledge-graph-index.summary: Graph index built by prompting an LLM to extract entities (nodes), relationships (edges), and covariates/claims from source text chunks, with duplicate relationships aggregated into edge weights — a form of abstractive summarization of the corpus.

leiden-hierarchical-community-detection.label: Leiden hierarchical community detection
leiden-hierarchical-community-detection.summary: Community-detection step that partitions the entity graph into nested modular communities of closely related nodes using the Leiden algorithm recursively, exploiting graph modularity to create a hierarchy from leaf-level to higher-level communities.

community-summaries.label: Community summaries
community-summaries.summary: Report-like summaries pregenerated by the LLM for each graph community, built bottom-up so higher-level summaries recursively incorporate lower-level element summaries; together they give global descriptions and insights over the corpus.

map-reduce-answer-generation.label: Map-reduce community answering
map-reduce-answer-generation.summary: Query-time procedure where each relevant community summary independently generates a partial answer (map step) and partial answers are combined into a final global answer (reduce step), distributing sensemaking across many context windows.

llm-judged-sensemaking-metrics.label: LLM-judged sensemaking metrics
llm-judged-sensemaking-metrics.summary: Head-to-head evaluation of free-form sensemaking answers via an LLM judge using Comprehensiveness, Diversity, and Empowerment criteria, with Directness as a control criterion that is expected to oppose comprehensiveness/diversity.

edges.evidence: The article and docs show code importing DistillationConfig and DistillationTrainer from trl.experimental.distillation and describe them as the way to run TRL distillation.
The article contrasts teacher-generated off-policy completions with student-generated on-policy rollouts scored by the teacher.
Docs describe DistillationTrainer as implementing on-policy knowledge distillation; the article states TRL now supports on-policy distillation with 100B+ teachers.
The article says the generation buffer batches prompts across gradient accumulation steps while preserving on-policy training because student weights stay fixed until the optimizer step.
The article says the buffer takes advantage of vLLM batching and reports speedups from 1.9x at grad_accum=2 to 41.7x at grad_accum=64.
The article moved the teacher to an external vLLM server so workers could query it for token log-probabilities.
The article describes an asyncio.Queue batching layer that drains requests every few milliseconds or on size/token limits and reduced tail latency by about 10x.
The article says nested JSON logprob lists were replaced by base64-encoded NumPy arrays, reducing payload size about 5x and improving client decoding from 436.4 ms to 17.0 ms.
The article explains that comparing full vocabularies is expensive and practical systems approximate KL using top-k log-probabilities; docs expose loss_top_k.
With top-k forward KL, token IDs are selected from the teacher's highest log-probabilities.
With top-k reverse KL, token IDs are selected from the student's highest log-probabilities; docs say beta=1.0 approximates reverse KL.
The article says 100B+ teachers such as Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 cannot be colocated with training GPUs, motivating an external teacher server.
The article reports that 235B and 30B Qwen teachers yield similar distilled 4B AIME25 results despite different teacher scores, interpreting this as a teacher-student capacity gap.
The article demonstrates transferring bushcraft/survival and math reasoning behaviors into smaller students using the described distillation setup.
Abstract frames GraphRAG as combining RAG and QFS strengths to scale with both the generality of user questions and the quantity of source text for global sensemaking.
Paper shows vector RAG fails on global questions over an entire corpus; GraphRAG is proposed to overcome this, achieving 72-83% comprehensiveness win rates over a vector RAG baseline.
GraphRAG first uses an LLM to derive an entity knowledge graph from source documents (stage 1 of the two-stage index).
The graph index (nodes, edges, covariates) is partitioned by Leiden community detection into nested communities the LLM can summarize.
Detected communities are summarized bottom-up into community summaries, with higher-level summaries recursively incorporating lower-level ones.
Each community summary is used to generate a partial response in the map step before partial responses are summarized into a final response in the reduce step.
GraphRAG answers queries through map-reduce processing of community summaries.
GraphRAG is evaluated head-to-head with an LLM judge on Comprehensiveness, Diversity and Empowerment, using Directness as a control criterion.
